entryPoint: io.legado.app.model.analyzeRule.AnalyzeUrl (constructor, 14 parameters) + getStrResponseAwait, driven inside the installed io.legado.app.debug process through reflection
capabilityRows: D default request headers (User-Agent, Keep-Alive, Connection, Cache-Control) and a source that declares each
D User-Agent: null, the frozen opt-out
D redirect chains 300/301/302/303 with a POST body, 307/308, content-header removal
D cross-origin Authorization drop, declared Cookie forwarding (recorded divergence)
D {{key}} raw substitution, the query encoded once, an already-encoded query left alone
D the exact bytes for { } | ^ ` \ ' spaces and non-ASCII
D {{page}} and <1,2,3> page lists, and the empty binding on a stage that carries no page
D declared GBK body bytes and 307 preservation, Content-Type charset precedence, and GBK form percent-encoding (v2 device run pending)
coverageGaps: The corpus drives AnalyzeUrl directly rather than the four WebBook stages, so a request the frozen WebBook builds with other arguments (a chapter body, a login header map) is not covered; the argument shapes it does use are the ones WebBook.kt:60 (search, key+page), WebBook.kt:169 (book info, no key/page), WebBook.kt:244 (toc, no key/page), BookChapterList.kt:70 and BookContent.kt:90 (next page, no key/page) construct.
The rows drive the frozen OkHttp path only (useWebView stays false, `type`/`upload` are not options this corpus sets), so the WebView request path (#2) is not covered.
No `retry` option row: the non-2xx retry loop (#9, OkHttpUtils.kt:29-43) is pinned by the product's own tests and is not re-opened here.

Version 2's three charset rows have no frozen device golden yet (#54: handset 5615f742 unavailable). The committed v1 golden and manifest remain historical evidence only; the comparator must reject their identity mismatch with v2.
The `escape` encoder, unknown charset labels, UTF-16 output, and characters a legacy charset cannot represent are outside these rows; the bridge retains its encoding_rs limits.

The redirect rows observe the requests the replay server receives; a Set-Cookie on a hop and other client-internal state are out of this corpus' scope (the differential contract's known-divergence row records the hop-cookie loss).
Only one response status shape per redirect status is exercised: the Location header is always relative to a declared origin, so a relative Location and a cross-scheme hop are not covered.
note: The rows drive io.legado.app.model.analyzeRule.AnalyzeUrl through reflection inside the installed frozen process, with the corpus' own in-process replay server on port 18731. Every row's evidence is the ordered request the server received (method, target, headers, body) plus the row's outcome. The corpus is the input only; the observed bytes belong to the golden. Rows whose `request.rule` carries a `,{...}` option object are declared exactly as a Book Source would declare them, so the method/body/header handling under test is AnalyzeUrl's own.
